extracted.intended_audience: teachers, education policymakers, students and scholars of education/philosophy of education
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on formulating and evaluating educational aims, methods, and curriculum for a democratic society, emphasizing social efficiency, civic competence, culture, interest, and discipline. Aims to help educators align instruction with individual capacities, social meaning, and democratic values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social efficiency (broad meaning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Social efficiency indicates the importance of utilizing native individual capacities in occupations having a social meaning rather than imposing subordination; it is attained by positive use of capacities, not by negative constraint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate into specific aims such as industrial competency and capacity to participate in shared activities. Avoid using 'social efficiency' to justify subordination or to accept existing inequitable economic conditions as final. Emphasize development that enables individuals to join freely and fully in common activities; include intelligent sympathy and good will as chief constituents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial competency (as part of social efficiency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons should be able to earn a living and manage economic resources usefully; education must not neglect such basic considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training must avoid fitting individuals in advance for definite industrial callings based on parental wealth or status. Because industries change rapidly, training should develop flexible capacities rather than overly specific vocational skills. Education should remediate unfair privilege and deprivation instead of perpetuating them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civic efficiency / Good citizenship
rubrics_metrics.description: Capacity ranging from being an agreeable companion to the ability to judge men and measures wisely and to take a determining part in making as well as obeying laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this aim to protect against abstract 'training of power at large' and remind that civic fitness includes varied qualifications. Guard against narrowing civic efficiency so that it would exclude scientific discovery or other socially valuable but not overtly civic activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of arts, recreation, and scientific work within social efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Social efficiency ultimately covers capacity to produce and enjoy art, capacity for recreation, and significant utilization of leisure, in addition to overt acts of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not confine social efficiency to material service; recognize scientific discovery, artistic production, and cultivated leisure as essential to social progress and efficient social life. Ensure education cultivates these capacities as part of social participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Culture as aim (personal cultivation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Culture means something cultivated, ripened, personal development in appreciation of ideas, art, and broad human interests; its outcome should be the development of distinctive personal qualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oppose conceiving culture as an 'inner' refinement divorced from social intercourse. Foster unique, incommensurable aspects of personality; seek distinction of personality rather than mediocrity. Culture and social efficiency should not be opposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of social efficiency and culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Social efficiency and personal culture are compatible and, properly understood, ought to be synonyms rather than antagonists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test any stated large educational end by whether it translates into procedures consistent with other ends. Avoid divorcing efficiency (as external product) from the enriching experience that constitutes culture; aim for education that cultivates socialized mind able to expand perception of meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Against materialistic definition of educational success
rubrics_metrics.description: Efficiency should not be measured solely by tangible external products; such products are by-products of education, not its primary aim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware of adopting external output as the sole criterion; this strengthens the false conception of culture as purely inner. Emphasize achieving distinctively valuable experiences and communicable meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest as a central educative principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Interest denotes (i) the active state of development, (ii) the objective results foreseen and wanted, and (iii) the personal emotional inclination that binds the learner to the object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize interest as the connecting force between present powers and remote aims. Distinguish genuine interest (connection to present powers and aims) from mere seduction or extrinsic inducements; genuine interest engages attention, leads to reflection, and sustains effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest should be intrinsic (not mere bait)
rubrics_metrics.description: Material is genuinely interesting when it is connected with present powers and purposes of the pupil; making material interesting by extraneous inducements is pedagogical 'softness'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find objects and modes of action connected with pupils' present capacities, needs, and preferences. Seek material that engages activity toward an aim rather than rely on artificial devices or pleasures to secure attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest as intermediary/middle conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Intermediate conditions—acts to be performed, difficulties to be overcome, appliances to be used—are of interest because they are between initial powers and the aim; making material interesting is leading learners to see these connections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design learning sequences that make clear how present activities lead to foreseen ends. If learners cannot perceive the 'between', material must be reframed to show its role in achieving the end rather than resorting to bribes or punishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline defined as deliberation and persistence
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline means power at command: the mastery of resources for carrying through actions; it involves foresight of results and the depth of hold the foreseen outcome has upon the person (will).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote disciplined persons who ponder ends, plan means, and endure in intelligently chosen courses despite distractions. Discipline is positive—developing executive power—rather than mere mortification, compulsion, or subjection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish true discipline from obstinacy and merely intellectual foreseeing
rubrics_metrics.description: Obstinacy is persistence without clear purpose; speculative foreseeing without deep personal grip yields flabbiness of will. True discipline requires considered ends that grip the person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid confusing mere persistence or stubbornness with discipline. Foster intellectual clarity about ends and emotional/volitional engagement so that deliberation leads to sustained action rather than perfunctory or brittle effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdependence of interest and discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Interest and discipline are connected: interest is necessary for deliberation and executive persistence; without interest deliberation is superficial and persistence weak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to secure persistence only by coercion or punishment that arouses mere physical excitation; aim to arouse reflective interest so that discipline stems from internalized understanding of ends and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter must be related to active lines of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter should not be isolated 'studies' complete in themselves but treated as factors in carrying forward active lines of interest; a topic is studied when it figures in realizing ends that concern the learner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange curriculum so that facts, skills, and principles are presented as conditions for achieving purposeful activities. For example, numbers become objects of study when they represent relations upon which practical purposes depend. Avoid presenting subjects as ends in themselves under the claim of 'disciplinary' value without showing specific tests of usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject the doctrine of formal/general discipline as an unquestionable justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Labeling a study 'disciplinary' has historically protected it from inquiry; the claim of general disciplinary value cannot substitute for showing how a subject meets specific needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require that subjects and methods meet concrete tests: demonstrate connection to learners' aims and capacities. If a subject fails to develop constructive power or intelligent self-direction, responsibility lies with curriculum/methods, not solely the pupil.
